items.title: Move config files and cache files to ~/.config/logseq for following the XDG Base Directory Specification.

labels.name: :type/feature-request
labels.description: Closed at will. Feature requests are in Logseq forum https://discuss.logseq.com/

items.body:
[The XDG Base Directory Specification (XDGBDS)](https://specifications.freedesktop.org/basedir-spec/basedir-spec-latest.html) unifies the location of commonly needed kinds of files, such as configuration files, data files, caches.

Now, the plugins and settings of Logseq located in `~/.logseq`. It would be nice to move `~/.logseq` to `~/.config/logseq` for following the XDG Base Directory Specification.

items.title: Aliases are duplicating in the graph view and the searching result

labels.name: :type/enhancement
labels.description: Enhancement to product. Does not affect the overall basic use.

items.body: ### What happened? I found the alias feature works in an unusual way, and after checking this issue https://github.com/logseq/logseq/issues/4342#issuecomment-1048049248 and the related discussion, I figured it out and think it's really nice. > this is actually a feature, not a bug : > * if [[aliaspage]] is empty, all links are redirected to [[sourcepage]] > * if [[aliaspage]] has a different content from [[sourcepage]],links are displayed as linked refs in the sourcepage > > you can read more about the implementation and arguments in this topic: [discuss.logseq.com/t/improve-implementation-of-aliases/81/8](https://discuss.logseq.com/t/improve-implementation-of-aliases/81/8) BUT, here is what I cannot figure out: - If there no content/page for some alias which means they're **identical** to the "source" and not in a link-and-backlink connection, why link all the alias to each other in the graph? And it makes no sense to link all the backlinks to them separately. This causes tons of duplications in the graph view and create a huge obstacle to figure out the real relationship among them. - Same for the searching result. Instead, you could only show the source node, and list all its alias beneath it. It will make the result way much clearer and may also alleviate the potential performance issues. I list some of my rough thoughts in the following. Please consider improving current graph view experience. Thank you. ### Reproduce the Bug Just preview a page with a couple of alias. ### Expected Behavior _No response_ ### Screenshots - For a set of alias nodes: - `test1` is the source file - `test2` and `test3` is alias to `test1` and has no content. - `testing` is alias to `test1` but has different content. - `foo1` is linked to source file `test1` - `foo2` is linked to alias `test2` - `foo3` is linked to alias `testing` - A possible alternative for the graph view: - Possible alternative for the search result: ### Desktop Platform Information - MacOS 10.15.7 - logseq 0.6.4 ### Mobile Platform Information _No response_ ### Additional Context _No response_

items.title: Electron version in use is outdated and marked insecure
items.body:
### Search first

- [X] I searched and no similar issues were found

### What Happened?

The current release 0.10.9 uses electron version 27 which reached EOL 2024-Apr-16. In the master branch electron version 31 is used which will reach EOL 2025-Jan-14, which is at the time of writing in 1 month.

That means that the current version of logseq already is insecure and the master branch will become insecure very shortly.

Therefore I recommend upgrading electron to at least version 33 which will reach EOL 2025-Apr-29 and creating a new release.

See https://www.electronjs.org/docs/latest/tutorial/electron-timelines

### Reproduce the Bug

1. Download current version
2. investigate dependencies
3. Download master
4. investigate dependencies

### Expected Behavior

Release version should have an electron version which still receives security updates.

```
#+title: Mixing
* Topics
- Roland [[id:01fb71c0-798f-4485-9a8f-c6259c126469][808]]
```

second.org
```
:PROPERTIES:
:ID:       01fb71c0-798f-4485-9a8f-c6259c126469
```

items.title: Tables creation command + autoformat
items.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
I use a lot of tables in my docs and notes. Unfortunately I find creating table in markdown complicated, especially when one wants to add a new column. 
Also, the raw text result is often ugly and difficult to read, unless spending a lot of time adding the right amount of `-` and spaces. 

This is a simple example I used to test table rendering in logseq:

```
|column1|column2|
|--|--|
|value1|value2|
```

**Describe the solution you'd like**
- A `/table`command that asks how many rows/columns should be created,
- An auto format adjusting the number of `-` and spaces depending on cell content when leaving block editing mode. This would yield:

```
| column1 | column2 |
|---------|---------|
| value1  | value2  |
```
- Keyboard shortcuts to insert new column to right or left based on cursor position.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
I don't know if this can be of any help but I use [this feature](https://github.com/yzhang-gh/vscode-markdown#github-flavored-markdown) from a super useful VSCode extension.

items.title: ctrl+w should not close app

labels.name: :type/enhancement
labels.description: Enhancement to product. Does not affect the overall basic use.

items.body:
In the desktop version (0.5.9, Linux), `ctrl+w` closes the app window which isn't useful (e.g. because Logseq does not minimize to the system tray). "Quit Logseq" already has the `ctrl-q` shortcut.

Also, it isn't mentioned in the Keyboard Shortcuts docs. (though `ctrl+q` isn't either, see #3966)

The `ctrl+w` shortcut seems to come from the electron default menu, see e.g. electron/electron#5951.

What should it do instead? Probably nothing at the moment, maybe "close tab" in case Logseq introduces tabs...
